panels.assertion_heading: The loudest possible whisper still cannot be heard
panels.narration: Could our universe have been born inside a black hole and kept its parent's spin like a birthmark? Think of a ceiling as the loudest a whisper could possibly be. We read all 4 published papers—the whole four-link chain—and calculated that ceiling. No observable signature survives. Even the loudest signal is about 10,000 to 100,000 times quieter than the best possible galaxy count, like a whisper buried under a stadium. The route stays closed. Here's how we got there.

panels.narration: Picture spacetime—space and time joined—as cloth woven from tiny compass needles. A particle's spin is a built-in quantum property—a rule at nature's smallest scales—like one needle's direction. Einstein-Cartan gravity is Einstein's gravity extended to include spin. In that theory, all those tiny twists can twist spacetime itself. That spacetime twist is called torsion. Our illustration lights the twist only after the cloth appears. This paper contains no plots—the entire argument is equations. So how could that faint twist reverse a collapse?

panels.assertion_heading: Torsion acts like a spring at the bounce
panels.narration: Squeeze a spring and it pushes outward. At crushing density, torsion—the spin-made twist in spacetime—is proposed to push the same way. A negative torsion density means an outward effect, not less than nothing. Collapse then turns into a bounce, a change from shrinking to growing. Today's estimate is roughly a negative 1 sitting 70 places after the decimal point—like one whisper against an unimaginably loud room. The no-plots card stays beside our spring illustration. But how do we add up countless tiny spins?

The printed value sits near the lined-up edge, so we carry both. What if a later correction changed the print?

panels.assertion_heading: The bounce neither smooths nor creates lopsidedness
panels.narration: Squeeze a balloon unevenly; one side bulges, the other flattens. Uneven squeezing is shear. Torsion, the spin-made spacetime twist, and shear change at the same rate as the universe changes size. The on-screen scale stays level. Their ratio, the comparison between them, is frozen. The bounce neither smooths nor creates lopsidedness. Any lasting memory depends on particle production—the creation of new particles—a step the papers assert but never derive. This is a condition, not a signal size. Can a real cosmic fossil hear anything this chain leaves behind?
